Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle. Quezon City http: l/www. dilg.gov.ph OPINION NO. Z_- VICE MAYOR MARIA NORLY T. PEPITO 03 MAY Office of the Sangguniang Bayan Impasugong, Bukidnon Dear Vice Mayor Pepito: This has reference to Resolution No. 2017-167 dated 9 October 2017 of the Sangguniang Bayan of Impasugong, Bukidnon, entitled "RESOLUTION SEEKING LEGAL OPINION FROM THE PROVINCIAL LEGAL OFFICER AND THE DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT, LEGAL DIVISION, REGIONAL OFFICE 10 REGARDING THE LETTER REQUEST OF THE MUNICIPAL MAYOR FOR AUTHORITY TO EXECUTE A DEED OFASSIGNMENT (DOA) TO THE IMPASUGONG ENERGY CORPORATION (IMECO) AND ASSIGN ITS INVESTMENTS AND ALL OTHER PERMIT'S GRANTED UNDER THENAME OF THE LGU-IMPASUGONG". The issues herein call to mind three salient provisions of the Local Government Code of 1991 (R.A. No. 7160): 1. Section 22 (c) of the aforementioned Code provides that: "Unless otherwise provided in this Code, no contract may be entered into by the local chief executive in behalf of the local government unit without prior authorization by the Sanggunian concerned. A legible copy of such contract shall be posted at a conspicuous place in the provincial capitol or the city, municipal or barangay hall. " 2. Section 444(b)(1)(vi) of the same Code evenly provides that the Municipal Mayor shall: "Upon authorization by the sangguniang bayan, represent the municipality in all its business transactions and sign on its behalf all bonds, contracts, and obligations, and such other documents made pursuant to law or ordinance. " 3. Section 447(a)(2)(iii) of the Local Government Code stating the specific powers and functions of the Sangguniang Bayan provides as follows: "Subject to the provisions of Book II of this Code and upon the majority vote of all the members of the Sangguniang Bayan, authorize the s. 20L

municipal mayor to negotiate and contract loans and other forms of indebtedness. "(Emphasis supplied) The foregoing rule leaves no doubt that prior authorization from the Sangguniang Bayan is necessary in order for the local chief executive to validly enter into contracts in behalf of municipality. However, when it comes to contracting loans and creating other forms of indebtedness, the authorization required from the Sangguniang Bayan, as expressly provided under Section 447(a)(2)(iii), is that approved by a majority vote of all the members of the Sanggunian. The majority vote of all the members of the Sanggunian is what in law known as Qualified Majority Vote. I Moreover, in the case of Vergara vs. Corona, et.a12, the Supreme Court affirmed the Order of the Ombudsman in OMB-L-C-02-1205 dated 22 August 2005, wherein, it was ordered that: " On the absence of ratification by the City Council of the MOA, Deed of Sale, Deed of Mortgage, and Deed of Assignment, respondents explained that Section 22M Republic Act No. 7160 (RA 7160) spoke of prior authority and not ratification. Respondents pointed out that petitioner did not deny the fact that Mayor Lajara was given prior authority to negotiate and sign the subject contracts. " Accordingly, the Department is of the considered view that the request for an authority of Mayor Anthony A. Uy from the Sangguniang Bayan members to execute a Deed of Assignment (DOA) to Impasugong Energy Corporation is well within the above- mentioned provisions of the LGC and the decided case of the Supreme Court. However, it must be emphasized that the voting requirements, that is Qualified Majority, as mentioned in Section 447(a)(2)(iii) must be properly complied with. With respect to the herein draft DOA, specifically the second WHEREAS Clause, we are of the opinion that the same is an implication of Section 302(a) of the Local Government Code (LGC), to wit: "Local government units may enter into contracts with any duly prequalified individual contractor, for the financing, construction, operation, and maintenance of any financially viable infrastructure facilities, under the build-operate-and-transfer agreement, subject to the applicable provisions of Republic Act Numbered sixty-nine hundred fifty-seven (R.A. No. 6957) authorizing the financing, construction, operation and maintenance of infrastructure projects by the private sector and the rules and regulations issued thereunder under such terms and conditions provided in this Section. " DILG Legal Opinion No. 050-09 dated 18 September2009 2 G.R. No. 174567, 12 March 2009

Build-operate-and-transfer (BOT) is a contractual arrangement whereby the project proponent undertakes the construction, including financing, of a given infrastructure facility, and the operation and maintenance thereof. The project proponent operates the facility over a fixed term during which it is allowed to charge facility users appropriate tolls, fees, rentals, and charges not exceeding those proposed in its bid or as negotiated and incorporated in the contract to enable the project proponent to recover its investment, and operating and maintenance expenses in the project. The project proponent transfers the facility to the government agency or local government unit concerned at the end of the fixed term that shall not exceed fifty (50) years. This shall include a supply-and-operate situation which is a contractual arrangement whereby the supplier of equipment and machinery for a given infrastructure facility, if the interest of Government so requires, operates the facility providing in the process technology transfer and training to Filipino nationals3. Since this Department was not furnished with a copy of the said Memorandum of Agreement, we considered the project herein as a BOT arrangement on the basis of the herein draft DOA. Nevertheless, please be reminded that a provision as to the profit-sharing agreement should be reflected in the MOA, as well as, who shall own the project/improvement upon the termination of the agreement. Lastly, it is understood that the terms and conditions contained in the draft DOA is within the discretion of the parties and that a legible copy of such DOA shall be posted at a conspicuous place in the municipal hall. We hope to have addressed your query accordingly. Very truly yours By A •ty of the Secretary: AUSTERE A. PANADERO Undersecretary cc: 2018- RD ARNEL M.
